note: [agent-bulk] Verdict is on the LEADING EM shower 10020 (193.5 MeV, 3 seg, pdg 11) and it is correct; the interesting finding on this event is on the SECOND shower 80061 and lives in the marks below. event_half_span_cm 123.5, so the r95 vertex sweep is fine and I did not re-capture with --vtx-span. VERTEX IS GOOD: on vtx-az-055-el+20 and vtx-az+065-el+20 the star is a clean five-prong fan and all five prongs touch it at 0.00 cm - 10015 (pdg 2212, 64.6 cm), 10026 (pdg 13, 114.6 cm), 10066 (pdg 211, 33.0 cm), 10017 (pdg 211, 24.3 cm), 10027 (pdg 211, 14.8 cm) - and every one of them is correctly left UNOWNED. SHOWER 10020: on shw10020-acc there are three member squares and exactly ONE non-member circle inside 65 cm, 10027 at (20.6 cm, 24.9 deg) - and 10027 is one of those vertex pions, a 14.8 cm track, so excluding it is right, not a miss. No grey EM-like charge inside 10020's cone. Its body is a single 24 cm segment plus two sub-1 cm specks at 19.2 cm / 19.3 deg and 49.3 cm / 14.1 deg: sparse, but sparse is not under-clustered (pilot section 2.3). SECOND SHOWER 80061 (113.8 MeV, 8 seg) IS OVER-CLUSTERED, and shw80061-acc makes it unmistakable: ONE member square at 0.5 cm and then SIX member squares bunched at 62-72 cm from the shower start at 10-23 deg, with NOTHING between 1 and 62 cm - a 55 cm empty gap inside one shower. The near part is the cluster-80 core (80061 4.6 cm + 80062 3.0 cm) sitting 30 cm from the vertex; the far part is a six-segment clump from clusters 36/37/50/51 about 95 cm from the vertex, every one of them pulled in by pass4_angle (direct), the late angle-only pass. A shower is contiguous; this member set spans two apexes. I marked the six far pieces OUT of 80061: 37030, 50050, 51055, 50047, 36029, 51056. All six are the same strength - they are one clump on the far side of one gap, so the owner reverses them together or not at all. THE SPLIT I AM NOT SURE OF, and it is the honest weakness of those marks: I chose to keep the cluster-80 core as 80061 and eject the far clump because pass4_angle is the mechanism that bridged the gap, but the far clump is the bigger object (about 20 cm of segments against the core's 7.6 cm) and the opposite split - the far clump is the real photon and the core is the intruder - fits the picture just as well. Reconciliation check (correction 11): nseg 8 and exactly eight segments carry owner 80061, so no segment here is silently shared with another shower. PI0: the reconstruction stored NO pi0 group. The display's auto-slotted pair 10020 + 80061 prices at 121.9 MeV on the vertex convention (theta 48.5 deg, inside the code's accept window) and 220.2 MeV on the axis convention, Epi0 307.3 MeV, asym 0.26 - so on the vertex convention this looks like a missed pi0 with two detached gammas. I deliberately did NOT store that pairing: gamma2's energy comes from a member set I have just called over-clustered, so pricing a pi0 off it would build on the thing I am disputing. If the owner ejects the far clump the pairing must be re-priced. NOT LOOKED AT: 10 of the 12 shower nodes were out of scope, all at 12.8 MeV or below (42035, 49042, 38031, 44037, 43036, 41034, 40033, 47040, 39032, 45038); one of them, 47040, carries the table flag 'conn 4: dropped by the PF tree'.
